empty.title: No services match
empty.text: Try another tab, group or filter.

hints.networkd-wait-online: You use NetworkManager, so you probably don't need it. Disabling it is safe.
hints.nm-wait-online: It only delays boot until a network is up. It is usually harmless if no network is connected at startup.
hints.resolved: DNS lookups may fail. Check that no other DNS service is using port 53.
hints.start-limit: It restarted too often and systemd gave up. Fix the cause in the log, then start it again.
hints.oom: It was stopped because the machine ran out of memory.
hints.timeout: It took too long to start or stop. Look at the log for what it was waiting for.
hints.exec-missing: The program could not be started. It may be missing or not executable; check the ExecStart line in the unit file.
hints.user-missing: The user or group the service should run as does not exist.
hints.env-setup: systemd could not prepare the environment for the service. The log has the details.
hints.cmd-not-found: A command it tried to run was not found. Check that its package is installed.

stop.title: Stop {name}?
stop.text: Stopping {name} could cut you off from this machine or break things that depend on it. Type its name to confirm.

disable.title: Disable {name} at boot?
disable.text: {name} will no longer start by itself when the machine boots. It could be something you rely on to sign in. Type its name to confirm.

mask.title: Mask {name}?
mask.text: A masked service cannot be started by anyone, not even by other services, until you unmask it.

info.memoryHistory: Memory use while this panel is open
info.sparkNote: Memory use since you opened this panel
info.bootHint: Starts this service automatically when the machine boots.

logs.error: The log could not be read
logs.emptyHint: If you expected some, your account may not be allowed to read the journal. Unlock administrator rights and try again.

unit.noFile: This unit has no file on disk.
unit.noOverrides: No overrides. The service runs exactly as its package defines it.
unit.removeText: The service goes back to the settings from its package. Your changes in override.conf are deleted.
unit.editNote: You are editing {path}. Only the lines you write here replace the package settings.
unit.applyNote: Changes apply the next time the service restarts.
unit.safeNote: The package's own unit file stays untouched, so updates will not overwrite your changes.
unit.error: The unit file could not be read

mask.text: Its start type will be set to Disabled: it will not start, not even when another service needs it, until you set it back to Manual.
